newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to double Russia gas import, boost transit.
newsitem.headline: Romania to double Russia gas import, boost transit.

text.p: Romania has signed an agreement to double annual natural gas imports from Russia to 14 billion cubic metres by the year 2005, industry ministry officials said on Monday.

"Our agreement with Russia aims at doubling Romania's natural gas imports and also boosting its transit capacity to Balkan countries like Bulgaria, Turkey and Greece," a senior industry ministry official, Cristian Istodorescu, told Reuters.

He said that the deal signed last week in Moscow by Prime Ministers Nicolae Vacaroiu and Viktor Chernomyrdin provides for imports of 14 billion cubic metres by 2005, nearly twice the current level of 7.2 billion.
The agreement called for investment of about $200 million in two new pipelines and two compressor stations to boost transit capacity of Russian gas to Bulgaria, Turkey and Greece.
A spokesman for Russia's Gazexport, a subsidiary of the giant Gazprom concern offered no comment on the deal.
Romania's natural gas consumption stands at an annual 26 billion cubic metres, including 19 billion produced domestically.

But production is expected to drop to aproximately 14 billion in the next decade. Onshore and offshore exploration in the Black Sea is being pursued, but the country is expected to remain highly dependent on Russian imports for years to come.
Forecasts show an increase in consumption to aproximately 30 billion cubic metres on the basis of an expected revival after the post-communist industrial production decline.
Romania's location gives it a significant role in transporting gas from the former Soviet Union to southeastern Europe and the potential to develop gas transit pipelines.
Istodorescu said contracts had already been signed with Bulgaria, Turkey and Greece. "But the deal is open for other Balkan countries too," he said.
He said the transit capacity of the new pipelines would be dictated by whatever agreements would be struck between Gazprom and its Balkan partners.
Bulgaria and Turkey currently receive some 20 billion cubic metres of Russian gas a year through pipelines which cross Romania, Istodorescu said.

Gazprom plans annual supplies in 2010 of 20 billion cubic metres for Turkey, four billion cubic metres for Greece, one billion cubic metres for Albania, two billion cubic metres for Serbia and one billion cubic metres for Macedonia.
